context.name: Context
context.audience: Anyone new to GOV.UK Chat, including non-engineers
context.blurb: GOV.UK Chat among the systems around it: the app a question is typed into, the AWS services that answer it, and the private repository that holds every prompt. C4 level 1 — runtime only.
context.note: Which caller reaches this system is not provable from either repository: the app backend forwards to whatever an SSM parameter names. Everything else here is read from this repository's own code.
context.dashMeans: a dependency resolved when the agent is built, not a call it makes

request.name: Request path
request.audience: On-call, and anyone tracing a question through the system
request.blurb: Every hop one question takes, numbered in reading order. The TypeScript API is the worked example because it has exactly one route, so the whole path is provable end to end.
request.note: Three gates before the agent runs: the Cognito scope, the schema, and the run claim that stops two answers being generated on one thread at once. The answer streams back along the same hops, so no return line is drawn.

containers.name: Containers
containers.audience: Chat engineers, and anyone reviewing a change to a stack
containers.blurb: Every separately deployable part the CDK app creates per environment, grouped by the stack that owns it, and the traffic between them. C4 level 2.
containers.note: There is no network layer to show. Nothing in this repository creates a VPC, a subnet, a security group or a VPC endpoint, so every call here is one AWS service reaching another over its public endpoint, authorised by IAM. Bedrock and the private prompts package are on Context, where the calls to them are set out.

security.name: Security
security.audience: Anyone reviewing what a caller, a function or an agent is allowed to do
security.blurb: The chain of authority on each API: what admits a caller, what the code then runs as, and what that identity may reach. Two chains, because the two APIs are guarded in completely different ways.
security.note: What is absent matters as much as what is present here, so the absences are listed rather than drawn. Nothing in this repository creates a customer-managed key, point-in-time recovery, deletion protection, a Web ACL, a log retention period, a tracing configuration, a Secrets Manager secret or an SSM parameter.

delivery.name: Delivery
delivery.audience: Anyone asking how a change reaches an environment
delivery.blurb: How a change gets deployed. Continuous integration checks and synthesises; it never deploys. The only thing in this repository that deploys is a script a person runs on their own machine.
delivery.note: No workflow here holds an AWS credential: there is no role to assume, no credential step and no OIDC token request anywhere in the workflows. The only secret any of them uses is the token for the private prompts repository. How staging and production are deployed is not visible in this repository.

resources.name: Resources
resources.audience: Cost, audit and incident scoping — the detail behind every badge
resources.blurb: Every AWS resource the CDK app declares, counted per environment by reading the constructs.
resources.note: Counts are read from the source, not synthesised. This repository's CDK app bundles every agent in Docker against a private git dependency, so nothing outside its own CI can synthesise it — which is also why no count here is gated by a build. Environments are ephemeral by default: only stag and prod are durable, and every other name, including a developer's own, gets its own copy of all four stacks.
